subject: Post-demo: Performance SLOs & Load Test Plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Performance SLOs & Load Test Plan

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment before the load test: 

Agreed performance targets from the call:
- P95 latency: <= 300ms (text generation endpoint, non-streaming)
- Streaming latency for chunk delivery: <= 150ms per chunk; consumer expects steady chunk cadence (~50 tokens/sec)
- Sustained throughput: 200 req/s for 30m windows; peak bursts to 400 req/s for up to 2m
- Concurrency: target 50 concurrent requester sessions with warm KV cache
- Error budget: <1% 5xx during test window; any spike >2% triggers immediate pause and triage

Load test approach you suggested: customer-led using k6 to hit our hosted API. We offered:
- a short-lived test account + API key for the run
- IP allowlist entries for your load generators
- a canary ramp then full run window and guidance doc (attached)

Ask from our side to keep things smooth:
1) Confirm the final test window (UTC) and your test IP ranges to allowlist
2) Share the exact k6 script and target RPS/concurrency plan (if you want us to pre-validate)
3) Let us know whether you’ll use streaming (SSE) or non-streaming endpoints for the bulk of the test

Attaching: redwood-loadtest-plan-v1.pdf (test plan + runbook)

Next step: Alex — can you send proposed window + k6 script? We can provision the API key and IP allowlist immediately once we have ranges.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

--
Redwood Inference | Make inference predictable and economical
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finwise.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLOs & Load Test Plan

Thanks Marissa — joined by Priya here. Confirming we want Redwood to validate the k6 run and provide the test account. Details from our side: 

- We'll run a staged test: 10m ramp to 200 rps sustained for 30m, 2m bursts to 400 rps, total duration ~45m.
- Concurrency: our script simulates 120 virtual users ramping to 200 concurrent sessions (we expect some idle waits in the script).
- Streaming: primary load will be non-streaming calls to the /v1/generate endpoint; we will run a small streaming-focused test (SSE) in a separate canary to validate chunk cadence.
- Error handling: script marks 5xx as failures; we will stop if 2% error threshold exceeded.

Proposed window: Tue Apr 13, 2026 02:00 - 06:00 UTC (canary at 02:00, full run at 03:00) — please confirm.

Attached: finwise-k6-script.js (our k6 script)

Also: IP ranges for our cloud load agents:
- 35.201.0.0/16
- 35.208.0.0/15

Let us know the temporary API key format (bearer token) and any special headers we should include.

— Alex
Alex Johnson
Principal SRE, Load Testing | FinWise
alex.johnson@finwise.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwise.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLOs & Load Test Plan

Alex — thanks for the details and the script. We provisioned a temporary test API key and created the test user account. Details below (please do not share the token beyond the test team):

API endpoint: https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
Temporary API key (expires 48h): rwd_test_ABC123_EXAMPLE
Required headers: Authorization: Bearer rwd_test_ABC123_EXAMPLE; Content-Type: application/json; X-Client-ID: finwise-loadtest
Streaming note: if you call the streaming endpoint (/v1/generate?stream=true) you'll receive SSE chunks; ensure your k6 variant supports EventSource or use our streaming SDK wrapper.

IP allowlist applied for the ranges you provided: redwood-ip-allowlist.txt (attached)
I've also attached a short k6-runbook.md with recommended ramp schedules and probes (circuit breaker thresholds, backoff). A couple of operational notes: 
- We'll create a dedicated Slack channel (#finwise-loadtest) and invite your on-call.
- We publish live metrics to the dashboard: https://redwood.app/monitoring/finwise-loadtest

Let us know if you want us to run a quick pre-validation (single 5m smoke at low RPS) on Monday.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-ip-allowlist.txt, k6-runbook.md
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finwise.com>

Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 08:05:00 +05:30
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLOs & Load Test Plan

Aditya — thanks for provisioning and for the runbook. The window on Tue Apr 13 02:00 - 06:00 UTC works for our ops team. We’ll do the canary at 02:00, then the full run at 03:00 as proposed. 

A couple quick confirmations: 
- We will use the non-streaming endpoints for the main run. We’ll kick off a 5m streaming canary to validate chunk cadence as discussed.
- If we observe >1% 5xx we will pause and escalate; if >2% we will stop the test and open an incident.
- Please confirm how Redwood would like failures reported (Slack + incident postmortem doc?); we prefer that any immediate operator alerts go to the Slack channel, and then we collect results in the attached CSV template.

Attached: finwise will share test results against load-test-results-template.csv after the run.

Thanks — Priya
